approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 1  Chapter 128
 
      MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 1060-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the education law and the public health law, in
        relation to the dispensing of self-administered hormonal contra-
        ceptives"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This legislation will allow hormonal  contraception  to  be  available
over-the-counter  at  pharmacies,  expanding  access  to  birth  control
throughout New York. Specifically, the bill authorizes  licensed  physi-
cians and nurse practitioners to prescribe and issue non-patient specif-
ic  orders to pharmacists to dispense self-administered hormonal contra-
ceptives to customers pursuant to rules issued by  the  Commissioner  of
Education. Pharmacists will be able to dispense this medication provided
they  provide  the  patient  with a self-screening risk assessment and a
fact sheet.
 
  I proposed authorizing pharmacists to dispense contraception over-the-
counter as part of a package to secure and expand access to reproductive
health care in my 2023 State of the State address and Executive  Budget.
I am pleased this legislation has now passed both houses of the Legisla-
ture.  However,  the bill as originally drafted would not go into effect
until eighteen months after it is signed into law. In light of  national
threats  to  reproductive  freedoms,  we simply cannot wait that long. I
have reached an agreement with the Legislature  to  ensure  this  legis-
lation  will  be  effective January 1, 2024, which balances the need for
the development of safety protocols and regulations with the urgent need
to make contraceptives more readily available.
 
  On the basis of this agreement, I am proud to sign this bill into law.

  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Relates to the dispensing of self-administered hormonal contraceptives; authorizes a licensed physician and a certified nurse practitioner to prescribe and order a non-patient specific order to a pharmacist licensed and located in the state for the dispensing of self-administered hormonal contraceptives.
